title: Stale reads caused by process pausing
body: In an Antithesis run against the main branch, one etcd member's revision stopped progressing for a long time, but the member continued accepting reads and writes. The resulting history is not linearizable. The run artifacts and variable report dump are available. The cluster used ETCD_SNAPSHOT_CATCHUP_ENTRIES=100, ETCD_SNAPSHOT_COUNT=50, and ETCD_COMPACTION_BATCH_LIMIT=10.

symptoms_visible: During an Antithesis run, one member's revision did not progress for a long time while it continued accepting reads and writes, and the recorded history failed linearizability validation.
N0.label: N0 stale reads reported

symptoms_visible: A put of key26/value 147 was reported at revision 3 by one client while other clients' watches reported that value at revision 155; inspection of the DB and WAL files did not reveal corresponding data corruption.
N1.label: N1 linearizability violation clarified

symptoms_visible: Antithesis logs show a transaction completing with proposed index 11, followed about 460 ms later by a range request that received read index 10 and did not observe the completed write.
The reproductions occur around injected container pauses, CPU throttling, and slowed or jammed network links.
N2.label: N2 ordered stale ReadIndex evidence collected

symptoms_visible: One of three Antithesis runs on the branch containing the initial leadership/select-race fix reproduced the same linearization failure.
N3_x.label: N3_x initial race fix aftermath

symptoms_visible: Instrumented logs show a follower timing out and retrying ReadIndex multiple times with the same read-request-id while the leader is stalled; the eventual response can carry the earlier cached commit index.
N4.label: N4 reused ReadIndex context isolated

symptoms_visible: Runs using a fresh ReadIndex request ID for every retry did not reproduce the violation: the initial fixed runs passed, additional copies of the periodic run passed, and CI recorded five consecutive passes without the failure.
N5.label: N5 mitigation verified under fault testing

symptoms_visible: The unique-request-ID mitigation is merged on main, cherry-picked to the supported 3.4, 3.5, and 3.6 release branches, and covered by a changelog update; repeated Antithesis and CI runs have not found the stale-read failure.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: What exact client operations demonstrate the linearizability failure?
Can you explain what the porcupine graph or client histories show?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Client-4's watch and client-6's operation record show key26/value 147 at revision 3, while other clients' watches report the same put at revision 155.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: All clients report the value at the same revision; only the graph rendering appears delayed.
The mismatched revisions involve a different key, but the same completed operation is still observed at incompatible revisions.

question_patterns: Do the persisted DB or WAL files show corruption or conflicting stored revisions?
What did offline inspection of the member data find?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Inspection of the database and WAL files found no relevant data issue, apart from an independently explained missing tombstone revision.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The DB contains a corrupt record and the WAL is truncated at the conflicting revision.

question_patterns: Did Antithesis statistical debugging highlight any code path?
Is there an initial code location worth instrumenting?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The statistical debug view highlighted kvstore.go around code that had previously been changed for issue #19179, although Antithesis warned that instrumented line numbers might differ.

edges.comment: The initial report, maintainer clarification, persisted-data inspection, and Antithesis statistical clue are folded into one simulated user side.

question_patterns: Can you instrument the write, range request, commit index, applied index, and ReadIndex path and provide the ordered timeline?
Does a read begin after a write completes and still receive an older read index?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. A transaction completed on etcd2 with proposed index 11 at 23.731, then a range request began on etcd1 at 24.193, about 460 ms later, but received read index 10 and did not observe the committed result. Additional ReadIndex debug logging was added to trace the path.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The read began before the transaction completed, so the returned older value is compatible with linearizability.
The read began 500 ms rather than 460 ms after the transaction completed and still received index 10.

question_patterns: Can timestamps across the Antithesis process logs be trusted for event ordering?
Are the write completion and read start timestamps generated from a common simulation timeline?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Antithesis confirmed that the time and ordering of these logs can be trusted.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The timestamps are collected independently and cannot establish whether the read started after the write.

question_patterns: What do the injected pause, throttle, partition, and clog faults actually do?
Which process and network faults surround the reproduction?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: A node pause performs docker pause for roughly two seconds and then unpauses it; throttle lowers a container's CPU quota; slowed partitions delay packets between groups; and a jam applies a throughput limit to one link.

edges.comment: Handler-requested instrumentation and timeline analysis are measurements, not fixes. Antithesis staff and etcd maintainers are folded into the simulated user side.

solution.intent: Treat the stale result as a race between the ReadIndex response and leadership-change notification, and change the select/leadership handling to avoid accepting the response from the wrong leadership epoch.
solution.concrete_example: Patch the linearizable read select so a leadership change wins over a concurrently available ReadState, then run Antithesis on that branch.

edges.comment: This was an actual early hypothesis and attempted fix. It was falsified when one of three Antithesis runs on the fixed branch reproduced the failure; the reporter explicitly retracted the celebration and later called the leadership theory an early bad guess.

question_patterns: Can you add logs through linearizableReadLoop, ReadIndex messaging, and raft readOnly to correlate request IDs, retries, queue entries, and returned indexes?
When the leader stalls, does the follower reuse the same ReadIndex request context on retries?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. The logs show etcd0 sending ReadIndex with request ID 3744633826720154659, timing out while the leader is stalled, and retrying multiple times with that exact same ID. The leader's readOnly bookkeeping had already cached and queued that context with an earlier commit index.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Every retry already uses a fresh request ID, and the stale index is returned for a context that appears only once.
The same request ID is reused on one retry instead of two retries, with the same stale cached-index behavior.
The numeric request ID differs between runs but is duplicated within each affected run.

edges.comment: The deeper instrumentation isolated request-context reuse. The associated raft analysis inferred that duplicate contexts interact unsafely with readOnly's map and ordered queue, allowing delayed acknowledgements and queue advancement to return an older cached index.

question_patterns: Please test the change that generates a fresh ReadIndex request ID for every retry for at least multiple long Antithesis runs.
Do periodic robustness tests and CI still reproduce the linearization failure after disabling request-ID reuse?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The initial fixed runs reported 0 of 4 reproductions. After merging, the periodic main-branch run was repeated in three additional copies and all passed. By March 4, CI had recorded five consecutive passes since March 2 without finding the failure.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: A long Antithesis run with fresh IDs reproduces the same stale read and linearization failure.
Four consecutive periodic runs pass instead of five, with no reproduction under the same injected faults.

edges.comment: These are handler-requested fault-test and CI measurements. Earlier short-run confidence had already produced a false positive, so repeated long-run verification is required before resolution.

solution.intent: Prevent etcd ReadIndex retries from reusing RequestCtx, merge the verified mitigation, backport it to all supported stable branches, and document it for the next patch releases.
solution.concrete_example: Generate a new requestIndex each time linearizableReadLoop retries ReadIndex instead of resending the same context. Merge PR #21399, cherry-pick it to release-3.4, release-3.5, and release-3.6, and include the fix in the changelog for the upcoming patch releases.

edges.comment: PR #21399 was merged after repeated fault-test validation, then cherry-picked to v3.4, v3.5, and v3.6. Changelog PR #21425 was submitted, and patch-release planning followed.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause: after a timeout or process stall, etcd's linearizable ReadIndex loop reused the same request ID/RequestCtx on retries; raft readOnly bookkeeping uses that context in its map and ordered queue, so duplicate requests and delayed acknowledgements could release an earlier cached commit index and permit a stale read.

Must ground the diagnosis in the collected evidence: a read began after the index-11 transaction completed but received read index 10, and deeper instrumentation showed repeated ReadIndex sends using the identical request ID while the leader was stalled.
Must prescribe the verified mitigation of generating a fresh ReadIndex request ID for every retry, with merge and backports to supported v3.4, v3.5, and v3.6 branches.

Must not settle on DB/WAL corruption, the highlighted kvstore code, or the initial select/leadership-change race fix; persisted data showed no relevant corruption and the race-fix branch reproduced the failure.

Must require repeated Antithesis or equivalent robustness-test verification before declaring resolution; a short initial run was previously misleading, while the accepted fix passed multiple periodic copies and five consecutive CI runs.

persona_hint.experience_level: Expert etcd maintainer and robustness-testing engineer. Comfortable reading raft internals, instrumenting Go code across etcd and raft, reconstructing distributed timelines, running long Antithesis simulations, reviewing fixes, and coordinating backports.
persona_hint.communication_style: Technical, evidence-driven, and collaborative. Shares raw timelines and instrumentation commits, openly retracts premature hypotheses, asks other maintainers for review, and insists on repeated long-running fault tests before considering a critical consistency issue fixed.
